end.summary:
Practised estimating a large collection using a group of 10 as a guide.
Made 8 attempts, with 2 unaided correct responses.
Identified an estimate near 40 for a collection of 43.
Initially used row length to judge quantity; later recognised that spreading the same 8 objects does not change the count.
Counting groups as individual objects remained unresolved; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ananya practised using a known group of 10 to estimate a larger collection and reached an estimate near 40 for 43. They first judged the longer row as having more, then corrected this after seeing that the same 8 objects were only spread out. The idea that four groups of 10 represent about 40 objects still needs practice. At home, show small groups of 10 and ask, “How many groups, and about how many objects altogether?”
